mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate over the prior 3 months compresses equity discount rates, generating positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as monetary policy eases.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods where FEDFUNDS declines by at least 0.1% over the prior 3 months.

mechanism_narrative: Unemployment rate exceeding 5.5% for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions that reduce consumer spending and corporate earnings, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE rises above 5.5% and remains above for 2 months
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances where UNRATE exceeds 5.5% for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous decline in housing starts (HOUST) and rise in unemployment (UNRATE) indicates weakening demand conditions that reduce corporate revenue growth expectations, driving negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint condition of declining HOUST and rising UNRATE occurs in 100+ instances over 5 years, but SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of those instances.

mechanism_narrative: During late-cycle expansion regimes with GDP growth exceeding 2.5% annualized, S&P 500 underperforms as valuations become stretched, resulting in negative forward 60-day returns.
failure_condition: In periods where GDPC1 growth exceeds 2.5% annualized, SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of cases over a 5-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained upward trend in non-farm payrolls (PAYEMS) over the prior 3 months supports consumer spending and corporate earnings, generating positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods where PAYEMS increases by at least 100k over the prior 3 months.

mechanism_narrative: Year-over-year CPI inflation exceeding 2.5% signals persistent inflation that may trigger monetary tightening, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances where CPIAUCSL YoY change exceeds 2.5%.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous decline in industrial production (INDPRO) and rise in federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) indicates supply contraction and monetary tightening that reduces corporate profit margins, driving negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint condition of declining INDPRO and rising FEDFUNDS occurs in 100+ instances over 5 years, but SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of those instances.

mechanism_narrative: During post-recovery regimes where industrial production rebounds by at least 3% from its trough, S&P 500 experiences strong momentum, resulting in positive forward 5-day returns.
failure_condition: In periods where INDPRO rebounds by at least 3% from its trough, SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 60% of cases over a 5-year rolling window.
